summary: Browser redirect payload distributed via CDN with rotating destination domain
details: The package's main file px.js is a browser-only script that injects a full-viewport iframe pointing at a hardcoded remote URL (https://mfmz.ohylze.cn/H.html?c=0gjr) and overlays a Chinese 'loading' mask, silently redirecting visitors of any site that embeds the script off to an author-controlled destination. The package has no Node functionality — there are no install lifecycle hooks and require() in Node would fail on `document` — so installing the package via npm does not itself harm the installing developer or build system. The harm surface is downstream: sites that pull px.js via jsDelivr (purge.jsdelivr.net/npm/px8my/px.js) execute the redirect against their end users. A shipped maintenance script (update_px8my.sh) rewrites the hardcoded redirect domain, bumps the version, runs `npm publish`, and purges the jsDelivr cache, confirming the package is operated as a rotating redirect channel where the destination host is changed over time to evade domain-based blocking.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
